translation_notes: 7 isolated .add() calls across 3 different graphs (onto, align, clean_kb) inside two loops plus one rewrite loop. Each becomes @graph <var> + +{ }, re-declaring @graph whenever the site switches graph (block-scope allows redeclaring @graph mid-suite, takes effect from that line to the end of the enclosing suite per declarations.md).

Two of onto's three .add() calls on the same iteration (rdf:type and rdfs:domain) share the subject priv_prop unconditionally, so they were merged into one +{ s p1 o1 ; p2 o2 } (add_run_shared_subject shape) rather than kept as two separate +{ } -- this does not fit add_isolated's own definition but is the honest, most-specific translation for that pair. The third (rdfs:range) is conditional on `not is_obj_prop` and stays a separate +{ }: `;` cannot express a conditionally-included predicate-object pair without restructuring, which is forbidden.
onto.add(...) and align.add(...) never share a subject VALUE across graphs (same Python variable, different target graph), so no further merging applies there.

Function reads/writes graphs via 6 file-path arguments, not a Graph parameter: fixture.ttl's single-file convention did not fit, so driver.py stages 3 read-only input fixtures (fixture_kb.nt, fixture_ontology.ttl, fixture_alignment.ttl) and one fresh temp dir of output paths per side, then compares the 3 written files by RDF isomorphism -- same oracle (corpus/405), adapted for a file-based entry point instead of a graph-argument one.
Verified the fixture is not a hollow green: corrupting one predicate in translated.ldpy (rdfs:domain -> rdfs:seeAlso) flips the check to FAIL on ontology_expanded.
optimization_notes: STATUS DRAFT, reason: this region's custom driver.py hard-codes original.py vs translated.ldpy (it calls _exec_ldpy on translated.ldpy and never reads RDFEVAL_SIDES), so `rdfeval check` returns FAIL ('driver compared None') for optimized.py and optimized.ldpy although the translated pair is OK. The driver was not modified. Equivalence of both optimized artefacts was proved separately with a scratch copy of the driver (same fixtures, same graph-isomorphism comparison of the 3 output files and of stdout) with only the right-hand file swapped: equivalent=true for both; a deliberate mutation (rdfs:domain -> rdfs:seeAlso in optimized.ldpy) turned it false (ontology_expanded not isomorphic), so the fixture is not hollow. The driver needs a RDFEVAL_SIDES-aware right-hand side (rdfeval.harness.sides_from_env) to turn this to final.

optimized.py: `kb = Graph().parse(...)` replaces the Graph();parse pairs and the ';' one-liners are split; the noisy-triple filter drops the str() calls and the line-continuation backslash (startswith takes a tuple of namespaces, reusing DBO/DBP/DBR); `align.triples((None, P, None))` becomes align.subject_objects(P); `set(kb.subjects()) | set(kb.objects())` becomes kb.all_nodes(); prop_name is inlined; URIRef(p_str) and URIRef(node_str) become p and node (already URIRefs, so the same term); the unused imports (RDF is kept, XSD and the duplicate import dropped) and the `: dict` annotation are removed.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: Namespace objects become `@prefix ... as NAME .` (PRIV, DBO, DBR, DBP, OWL, still available for bind()/startswith); PRIV[x] becomes priv:{x}; align.subject_objects(P) becomes m{ ?s P ?o }(align); each onto.add/align.add becomes +{ }(graph) with the call suffix, so the @graph onto / @graph align switches of translated.ldpy disappear; only clean_kb needs a @graph declaration.

Exception to symmetry, island only: the rdf:type and rdfs:domain triples on the same priv_prop merge into one +{ ; } (Python has no shared-subject add). The conditional rdfs:range triple stays a separate +{ } because ';' cannot include a pair conditionally.

Not compressed: the noisy-triple removal still collects then calls kb.remove(t) (t is data, -{ } cannot take it); the translation_map is not merged with aligned_* (the maps differ when an aligned entity is absent from the KB); onto.bind/align.bind calls kept so the serialised prefixes are unchanged.
